unitObjectives.objective: Pupils will be able to describe how global warming causes Arctic ice melting using cause-and-effect connectors ('because' and 'so').
Pupils will be able to read and interpret stanzas of the narrative poem 'The Bear and I', identifying imagery, rhythm, and moral change.
Pupils will be able to compare traditional gasoline cars with clean vehicles (biofuel, electric, air, solar) using comparative adjectives ('cleaner', 'quieter', 'more expensive').
Pupils will be able to pronounce and spell words with the final consonant blend '-ng' (/ŋ/ sound: sing, long, reading, bang, spring).
Pupils will be able to use 'instead of' to express eco-friendly vehicle choices ('clean cars use electricity instead of gasoline').
Pupils will be able to complete a vehicle comparison matrix and write 4 sentences on environmental protection.

I can read aloud lines from the poem 'The Bear and I'.
I can compare an electric car and a gasoline car.
I can read and spell words ending with '-ng' like sing, spring, and reading.
I can explain how clean cars help protect the world.
I can use 'because' and 'so' to explain why things change.

reading.objective: Interpret poetic stanzas and compare informational science texts using classification tables.

listening.objective: Listen to scientific facts about clean cars and identify vehicle attributes from audio cues.

speaking.objective: Recite poetic stanzas chorally and debate the advantages and drawbacks of different car types.

writing.objective: Complete the Car Features Matrix on page 54 and write a 4-sentence comparison paragraph.

vocabulary.objective: Acquire and use 12 highlighted Words in Context and 12 supporting science words.

grammar.objective: Form comparative adjectives (short + -er vs more + long) and connect clauses with 'because', 'so', and 'instead of'.

phonics.objective: Articulate the voiced velar nasal /ŋ/ at the end of syllables without a hard 'g' click.

content.objective: Understand how burning fossil fuels creates dirty air and climate change, and how clean energy protects habitats.

thinking.objective: Compare and contrast attributes and trace multi-step environmental cause-and-effect chains.

values.objective: Develop environmental stewardship, empathy for vulnerable animals, and respect for green innovation.

readings.title: The Bear and I
readings.mainIdea: An Arctic fisherman and a hungry polar bear experience mutual danger and truce when thin sea ice cracks beneath them.
readings.summary: An Arctic fisherman tells a story from when he was young in a land of wind and snow. While fishing through an ice hole, he meets a giant polar bear twice his size. For many years, the bear was his hungry enemy at the fishing hole. But after many warm winters, the sea ice became thin. One morning, the ice cracked and both fell into the freezing water. Trapped by the broken ice, the bear and the man were not enemies; they helped each other survive. Today, as the ice continues melting, the elderly fisherman hopes to see the bear once more.

keySentences.sentence: I'm from a land of wind and cold / With fields of ice and snow. / My story starts when I was young, / Many years ago.
After many warm winters, / The ice on the sea was thin. / One morning, the bear was near me, / Crack! The bear and I fell in.
From that day on, it was clear, / Things change as years go by. / There is danger in this changing world, / For the bear and I.

readings.title: Clean Cars
readings.mainIdea: Traditional gasoline cars pollute the air and warm the earth, but clean cars (biofuels, electric, air, solar) help create a clean world.
readings.summary: Cars are everywhere, taking us to work, school, and vacation. However, traditional cars burn gasoline from crude oil, which is noisy and makes the air dirty, changing our climate. Today, scientists and engineers have built clean cars. Biofuel cars run on plant fuels like corn. Electric cars run on rechargeable batteries; they are fast, quiet, and produce zero smoke, though they are expensive. Compressed air cars are quiet and clean, but small and slow. Solar cars get clean energy from the sun. Clean cars are an essential way to protect our planet.

keySentences.sentence: Gasoline cars are fast, but they are noisy and make the air dirty. Dirty air is bad for animals, plants, and people. It changes our climate, too.

Clean cars are one way to have a clean world.

pageActivities.exactInstructions: Explore the Reading. A Look and read. Find words in the reading and label the cars. B Read and complete the table using these words. Use some words more than once. (quiet, dirty, clean, small, expensive, fast, slow, noisy). C What's the main idea of the article? Read and check (✓). D Think and discuss. Which clean car is your favorite? Why?
items: Car labeling: gasoline car, biofuel car, electric car, air car, solar car
Table: Type of car | Good things | Bad things
Main idea check: 1 Some cars noisy... / 2 Clean cars are good for the world. / 3 We need cars...
Sentence starter: 'I like the solar car because it is clean and quiet.'
pageActivities.answerKey: A: 1 gasoline car, 2 biofuel car, 3 electric car, 4 air car, 5 solar car; B: gasoline: fast / noisy, dirty; biofuel: fast, only little dirty / noisy, needs big fields; electric: fast, quiet, clean / expensive; air: quiet, clean, not expensive / small, slow; solar: clean, quiet, fast / expensive; C: 2 Clean cars are good for the world.
pageActivities.skill: Classification table completion & main idea check

pageActivities.exactInstructions: Think Together: UNIT 3. How can we make good changes in our world? A Think and write. What problems does climate change make for people and animals? B Think and discuss. What changes can you make to keep our world clean? Do a Numbered Heads Together routine. My Reading Journal check. Prompt: How does this unit make you feel? Write and draw how you feel.
items: Problems for People vs Animals
Numbered Heads Together: 'I can clean up trash because trash is dangerous for animals.' / 'I can ride a bike to school because bikes don't make the air dirty.'
Self-check checkboxes: polar bears, life in the Arctic, clean cars, climate change
Feelings prompt: 'I feel...'

Recite the stanza with rhythm and feeling.

praisePhrases.phrase: You are a wonderful planet protector!

fromUnit1And2.note: Connecting wildlife habitats to climate change.

canDoChecks.check: Can recite 2 stanzas of 'The Bear and I' with clear rhythm.
Can explain why sea ice melts.
Can compare two cars using 'quieter than' or 'cleaner than'.
Can name 3 clean energy sources for cars.
Can pronounce words ending in '-ng' without hard 'g'.
Can complete the Car Features Matrix on page 54.
Can state why the bear was not an enemy in the water.
Can form a sentence with 'because' explaining climate action.
Can identify the main idea of 'Clean Cars'.
Can write 4 comparison sentences using sentence frames.

oralCheck.question: Where does the fisherman fish in the poem?
oralCheck.expectedAnswer: In an ice hole in the Arctic.

oralCheck.question: Why did the ice crack under the bear?
oralCheck.expectedAnswer: Because the winters were warm and the ice was thin.

oralCheck.question: Which car is quieter: a gasoline car or an electric car?
What do solar cars use for energy?
oralCheck.expectedAnswer: They use energy from the sun.

speakingRubric.developing: Speaks with fragmented single words; omits 'than' in comparisons ('electric quiet').
speakingRubric.proficient: Uses comparative adjectives accurately ('cleaner than', 'quieter than'); explains causes with 'because'.
speakingRubric.advanced: Speaks fluently in full complex sentences; connects clean energy directly to Arctic animal survival.

writingRubric.developing: Writes incomplete phrases; misclassifies cars in the feature table.
writingRubric.proficient: Completes the Car Features Matrix accurately; writes 2-3 comparison sentences using sentence starters.
writingRubric.advanced: Produces a cohesive 4-sentence comparison paragraph with correct comparative adjectives and punctuation.

supportWeaker.description: Green block for 1-syllable + er (clean-er), purple block for more + long word (more expensive).
Have pupils touch their throat to feel nasal vibration for '-ng' without a final click.

challengeStronger.description: Design an experimental clean car and present 3 reasons why it protects the planet.
Write a 4-line rhyming stanza continuing the fisherman's story.

lessonSequence.title: The Pink River: Climate & Planet Changes
lessonSequence.objective: Pupils will be able to observe changes in nature and discuss the pink river.

stages.activity: Show the pink river photo on page 40; ask pupils what they see.
Explain scientist meltwater experiments; introduce Unit Big Idea.
Page 41 Wonder routine: pupils share good and bad changes in nature.
Pairs contrast the Arctic photo setting with where they live.
State one thing you see in the photo.

lessonSequence.title: The Ice Hole: Meeting the Giant Bear
lessonSequence.objective: Pupils will be able to read stanzas 1-4 and learn Words in Context.

stages.activity: Listen to Arctic freezing wind sound effect.
Read stanzas 1-4; introduce Words in Context box on page 43.
Vocabulary definition matching and TPR gestures.
Choral reading of stanzas 1-4 in groups.
Say how big the bear was ('twice my size').

lessonSequence.title: Crack! The Ice Trap & Truce
lessonSequence.objective: Pupils will be able to read stanzas 5-8 and explain the moral change.
targetChunks: The bear was not my enemy
made a trap for us both
lessonSequence.grammar: Past simple and negation (was not my enemy).

stages.activity: Review stanzas 1-4; mimic bear footsteps on thin ice.
Read stanzas 5-8 on pp. 44-45; analyze the ice crack and falling in.
Discuss: Why was the bear not his enemy in the water?
Expressive recitation of the final stanza.
Ask: 'Why did the ice crack?' (thin ice, warm winters)

lessonSequence.title: Poetry Check, Phonics -ng & Vehicle Intro
lessonSequence.objective: Pupils will be able to answer True/False, practice -ng phonics, and compare cars.

stages.activity: Choral recitation of key poem lines.
Page 46 True/False & Phonics -ng; contrast thin / thing.
Page 47 Compare and Contrast chart (Bear vs Man).
Compare red car and white car: 'Which car is cleaner?'
Pronounce two words ending in '-ng'.

lessonSequence.title: The Trouble with Gasoline: Dirty Air
lessonSequence.objective: Pupils will be able to explain how gasoline cars cause dirty air and climate change.

stages.activity: Listen to noisy highway traffic sounds.
Read pp. 48-49; introduce Words in Context box on page 49.
Sentence matching: gasoline comes from underground oil; causes smog.
Write 2 problems caused by gasoline cars in notebooks.
Ask: 'Where does gasoline come from?' (oil in the ground)

lessonSequence.title: Biofuels & Electric Power: Green Wheels
lessonSequence.objective: Pupils will be able to explain how biofuel and electric cars work.
lessonSequence.grammar: Contrast with 'but' and substitution with 'instead of'.

stages.activity: Show corn plant and battery; ask how they can power a car.
Read pp. 50-51; plant biofuels vs rechargeable batteries.
Sentence builder on board comparing electric and gas cars.
Pairs discuss: 'Electric cars are clean, but they are expensive.'
State one good thing about electric cars (clean and quiet).

lessonSequence.title: Air & Solar Power: The Clean World Goal
lessonSequence.objective: Pupils will be able to describe air and solar cars and complete the classification matrix.
targetChunks: Clean cars are one way to have a clean world
I like the solar car because...

stages.activity: Look at photo of solar racing car on page 53.
Read pp. 52-53; examine air cars and solar cars.
Complete page 54 Car Features Matrix in notebooks.
Complete sentence: 'I like the solar car because it is clean and quiet.'
Check Main Idea: Clean cars are good for the world.

lessonSequence.title: Protecting Our Planet: Action Showcase
lessonSequence.objective: Pupils will be able to formulate climate actions and complete self-check.
targetChunks: I can ride a bike to school because
I can clean up trash because

stages.activity: Choral reading of core slogan: 'Clean cars are one way to have a clean world.'
Examine page 55 Numbered Heads Together routine.
Group discussion: What changes can you make to keep our world clean?
Pupils complete self-check in My Reading Journal.
State one clean change before line-up.
